observations: The page number «59» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. At the foot, the signature «8*» on the right. L01-L03: «Die letztere Regel», al-Battānī's second rule for the argument of latitude, the true place of the node subtracted from that of the moon (p. 58, JP2 0090, L35-L37).

L10-L32: the computation is set in two columns: on the left the two ways to the argument of latitude (L10-L22), on the right the longitude of the node (L23-L32), transcribed one after the other. In the left column the figures stand at the left and the words after them; a rule under 279° 41′ (L12), under — 360° (L15) and under 80° 19′ (L19); L13, «kopfes», the end of the word divided in L12, stands about 20 px higher than «598° 43′» (L14), at the right of the rule. In the right column the figures stand in a column at the right; the ditto marks „ of L27-L28 under «für»; a rule under 45′ (L28).

L10-L32. Checked: the true place of the moon of p. 45 (JP2 0077, L33-L34), 319° 1′ 35″, rounded (note 3) is 319° 2′; 92° 39′ + 184° 42′ + 1° 35′ + 45′ = 279° 41′; 360° − 279° 41′ = 80° 19′; 319° 2′ + 279° 41′ = 598° 43′, less 360° 238° 43′; 319° 2′ − 80° 19′ = 238° 43′. With Brahmagupta's parameters (232 311 168 revolutions of the node in 1 577 916 450 000 days, see p. 42, JP2 0074) the node moves 184° 41′ 49″ in the 29 years, 10277 days, 1° 35′ 24″ in thirty days and 44′ 31″ in fourteen days, rounded 184° 42′, 1° 35′ and 45′, the values of L26-L28.

L33-L36: the end of the sentence and the result are set as a small table: «= 3° 48′ 57″» and «= 1′ 46″» with their signs of equality one under the other, a rule under «1′ 46″», and L36 «Breite des Mondes zu der gegeb. Zeit :» indented, «Breite» in italics. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; the empty cells give the columns room and are not printed. L34: «7s 28°», the s raised.

L33-L40. Checked: seven signs and 28° are 238°; 3° 48′ 57″ + 1′ 46″ = 3° 50′ 43″; 1′ 46″ is 43/60 of 2′ 28″, the change of the latitude from 238° to 239° by either of the rules below. For the argument 238° the formula of p. 58 (JP2 0090, L28-L30) with 4° 30′ gives 3° 48′ 54″ and 4° 30′ times the sine of the argument 3° 48′ 58″; the table's 3° 48′ 57″ lies between them. The argument 238° lies between 180° and 270°, where the latitude is south and growing towards the southern limit at 270°, as L37-L40 say. The values of Table 25 are to be compared with the table.

L04-L07: the greatest latitude of the moon: al-Khwārizmī and the Sūrya-Siddhānta 4° 30′, Ptolemy and al-Battānī 5°. L05: a grey mark below the degree sign of «90°», lighter than the print; not transcribed.

L41 and L42: the dashes of «21—26» and between the two headings are each printed in two pieces (17 and 22 px, 21 and 23 px, with gaps of 2-4 px); each transcribed as one long dash. Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Kh.», «Batt.», «Ptol.», «Burgess»; italics: «Sūrya-Siddhānta», «Shāh», «Siddhāntas», «Beispiel», «Breite» (L36), «südlich», «wachsend,», «Latitudo lunae recedentis,», the headings of L41-L43, «Computatio» (L45), «examen».
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (9-15 px measured).
